artists.biography: Goodbye Mr. Mackenzie was a late 1980s and early 1990s band which hailed from Bathgate, near Edinburgh, Scotland. It featured Martin Metcalfe as lead vocalist, John Duncan on guitar, Rona Scobie on keyboards, Fin Wilson on bass guitar, Derek Kelly on the drums and most notably, Shirley Manson (later of Garbage) as a keyboard player and background vocalist. perplexity.description:
Fish Heads and Tails is a compilation album by Scottish rock band Goodbye Mr. Mackenzie, released in November 1989 on Capitol Records. Comprising 10 tracks with a total runtime of approximately 40 minutes, the album functions as a mid-price collection drawing from the band's live performances and B-side material recorded between 1987 and 1989.

The album arrived during a transitional period for the band, following the moderate commercial success of their debut Good Deeds and Dirty Rags (1989), which had reached No. 26 on the UK Albums Chart. Released while Goodbye Mr. Mackenzie relocated to Berlin to record their second studio album, Fish Heads and Tails served as a stopgap release that allowed Capitol Records to maintain the band's profile during this creative shift. The compilation captures the group's rock-oriented sound from their early career, preserving material that might otherwise have remained obscure to casual listeners.

As a budget-priced compilation of live recordings and B-sides rather than a full-length studio album, Fish Heads and Tails occupies a secondary position within the band's discography. While such compilations typically generate limited critical attention, the release remains a documented artifact of Goodbye Mr. Mackenzie's formative years, offering insight into their working methods and the breadth of material produced during their initial Capitol Records period.
